web_title: 7. Why the Price Is What It Is: Valuation, Reverse DCF & Peer Comps
book_title: Chapter 7: Why the Stock Trades Here — Market Expectations vs. Peers
question: What future growth and margin durability is embedded in APARINDS's ₹59,408 Cr market cap at ₹14,250, and how does that compare to listed electrical peers after stripping out Q2's TSO windfall?

epigraph.quote: Price is what you pay; value is what you get. When a cyclical-margin compounder is priced for peak windfall spreads, even a strong industrial franchise becomes a fragile stock.
epigraph.author: Institutional Valuation Desk Maxim

web_blocks.html: At the live November 25, 2026 TradingView close of ₹14,250.00 (November 23 NSE daily OHLCV ledger close ₹14,184.00), Apar Industries commands a ₹59,407.94 Cr market cap (Screener: ₹59,660 Cr) [1, 26, 28]. Trailing twelve-month (TTM) net profit stands at ₹1,377 Cr through September 2026 [1]. The stock trades at 41.83x TTM P/E (Screener: 42.6x) and 7.00x P/B on post-QIP book value [1, 26]. On FY26 audited earnings (₹977 Cr PAT), the trailing multiple exceeds 60x [1].

Why does an industrial maker still trade above 41x earnings after a -26.03% drop from ₹19,265? First, H1 FY27 PAT jumped to ₹914 Cr (Q1 ₹467 Cr + Q2 ₹447 Cr), nearly matching all of FY26 [1]. Second, the August 2026 ₹2,500 Cr QIP lifted equity to ₹8,520 Cr, cut debt-to-equity to 0.12x, and earned a CARE AA; Stable upgrade [1, 22, 26]. Yet Pass 1 exposed a valuation trap. Fully 67% (+₹194 Cr of +₹288 Cr YoY) of Q2 post-forex EBITDA growth came from a one-off Specialty Oils windfall (₹23,262/KL on -20% volume) [21, 23]. Management warned those margins are 'by no means normal' [21]. Meanwhile, Q2 conductor volume fell 9.2% YoY, premium mix eased to 39.4%, and U.S. sales fell 29.7% YoY [21, 23].

We run a 10-year Reverse DCF on an enterprise value near ₹59,250 Cr (₹59,408 Cr market cap plus ~₹1,014 Cr debt, less ₹1,171 Cr cash) [22, 26]. We apply an 11.5% WACC (7.0% risk-free, 5.5% ERP, 0.89 beta) and 5.0% terminal growth. From a normalized ex-windfall NOPAT base of ~₹1,360 Cr, ₹14,250 implies 19.4%–20.5% annual FCFF growth for ten years.

web_blocks.caption: APARINDS Reverse DCF Sensitivity Matrix (Implied Fair Value per Share at 11.5% WACC, 5.0% Terminal Growth)
web_blocks.takeaway: At ₹14,250, the market prices in ~19.6% 10-year FCF compounding on TSO-inflated trailing earnings. Stripping out Q2's TSO windfall places present intrinsic value near ₹12,300—reconciling cleanly to a 12–18 month blended Base Target of ₹13,800.

web_blocks.caption: APARINDS vs. Indian Electrical Cables & Grid Equipment Peers (Live TradingView Snapshot, 25 Nov 2026)
web_blocks.takeaway: APARINDS trades at 41.83x TTM P/E—an 18.5% premium to Polycab (35.29x) and a 26.4% premium to KEI (33.09x), despite Polycab earning higher 33.2% ROCE and 12.65% OPM. Critically, all five electrical peers (APARINDS, POLYCAB, KEI, TARIL, TDPOWERSYS) are in Stage 4 markdown.

web_blocks.mechanism: Both European cable leaders saw multi-year EBITDA/MT expansion as offshore wind and HVDC interconnects created supply bottlenecks, lifting P/E multiples from 14x–16x to 22x–26x before project-timing pauses triggered 20%–30% pullbacks.
web_blocks.outcome_numbers: Prysmian grew EBITDA from €976M (2021) to >€1.9B (2024), yet suffered two 18%–25% valuation drawdowns whenever permitting slowed.
web_blocks.lesson_for_symbol: Even in a genuine grid supercycle, high-multiple industrials rarely move in a straight line; paying 41.8x peak-windfall P/E invites sharp de-rating during export and margin normalization.

web_blocks.html: DCF-to-Target Reconciliation: Compounding our ₹12,300 present-value DCF forward ~12 months at 11.5% WACC yields ~₹13,715—matching 33.25x normalized FY28E EPS (₹415) = ₹13,800 Base Target (in line with KEI at 33.09x and below Polycab at 35.29x). At ₹14,250, Base return is -3.16%.

web_blocks.title: Valuation Verdict: Reconciled DCF & Peer Multiples Show Negative Near-Term Upside
paragraphs: Rather than stretching for a 37.5x premium multiple while cable peers trade at 33x–35x in Stage 4, we anchor our 12–18 month Base Target at ₹13,800 (33.25x normalized FY28E EPS of ₹415). That sits squarely in line with KEI (33.09x), below Polycab (35.29x), and reconciles directly with our ₹12,300 present-value DCF rolled forward one year at 11.5% WACC.

Our Bear Target drops to ₹9,600 (26.3x Bear FY28E EPS ₹365, matching our 13.5% DCF Bear exactly), while Bull sits at ₹17,500 (38.5x Bull FY28E EPS ₹455, matching our 22.5% DCF Bull). Paying 41.83x trailing windfall earnings offers negative expected return.

book_paragraphs: Now that we have completed our forensic audit of Apar Industries without looking at the ticker, let us confront the market's price tag. At the live November 25, 2026 TradingView close of ₹14,250 per share (November 23 NSE ledger close ₹14,184), Apar carries a ₹59,408 Cr market cap—41.83 times trailing twelve-month earnings and 7.00 times post-QIP book value.

At first glance, a 26% pullback from the ₹19,265 52-week high might look like a bargain on a company that just reported ₹914 Cr of net profit in six months. Look closer, however, at what Pass 1 uncovered inside Q2 FY27. Fully two-thirds of the quarter's post-forex EBITDA expansion came from an abnormal Transformer & Specialty Oils margin spike to ₹23,262 per kiloliter on 20% lower physical volume—a windfall management explicitly warned is by no means normal. Meanwhile, physical conductor volumes declined 9.2% year-over-year, premium conductor mix slipped to 39.4%, and U.S. revenue fell 29.7%.

That earnings-quality distortion makes a 41.83x trailing multiple far more demanding than it appears on a screener page. In our 10-year Reverse DCF at an 11.5% WACC and 5.0% terminal growth, ₹14,250 assumes Apar compounds normalized free cash flow at nearly 19.6% annually for a full decade. Compare that with India's premier listed cable peers on the exact same session: Polycab India trades at 35.29x trailing earnings on a 33.2% ROCE, and KEI Industries trades at 33.09x. Apar trades at an 18% to 26% valuation premium to both, even though half of Apar's sales remain tied to conductors and oils.

Equally important, every single peer in our electrical table—Polycab, KEI, Transformers & Rectifiers, and TD Power Systems—is currently in Stage 4 markdown alongside Apar. The market is systematically repricing the entire Indian grid-equipment complex for slower near-term export conversion and normalizing spreads.

Pause for a moment to appreciate how much cash-flow realism changes the valuation math. On audited FY26 figures, Apar generated ₹22,902 Cr in revenue and ₹977 Cr in net profit, which puts the current ₹59,408 Cr market cap above 60 times full-year FY26 earnings. Even after giving full credit for H1 FY27's rapid expansion to ₹25,605 Cr in trailing twelve-month revenue and ₹1,377 Cr in trailing net profit, investors must remember that ₹194 Cr of Q2's ₹288 Cr post-forex EBITDA gain came from Specialty Oils rather than repeatable conductor or cable execution. Once you strip out that abnormal ₹23,262/KL oil spike and normalize TSO back toward ₹6,500/KL, the headline 41.83x P/E immediately expands into the mid-to-high 40s on repeatable operating profit.

Now layer the balance-sheet reality onto that multiple. The August 2026 ₹2,500 Cr QIP was a smart, timely move that lifted total equity to ₹8,520 Cr, brought formal borrowings down to roughly ₹1,014 Cr against ₹1,171 Cr in cash, and earned a CARE AA; Stable upgrade. Yet CARE Ratings also disclosed that FY26 working-capital requirements had climbed to ₹8,520 Cr—roughly 37% of operating income—pushing pre-QIP non-fund-based bank limit utilization to 88%. Earmarking ₹1,875 Cr (75% of QIP proceeds) for working capital stabilized the franchise, while H1 FY27 operating cash flow still printed at -₹862.63 Cr as ₹800 Cr of U.S. DDP shipments sat in ocean transit.

That is why valuation cannot be divorced from capital intensity. Polycab earns a 33.2% ROCE and 12.65% operating margin at 35.29x earnings, while KEI trades at 33.09x with a 0.05x debt-to-equity ratio. Paying 41.83x for Apar while conductor volumes are down 9.2% YoY, U.S. sales are down 29.7% YoY, and post-IBC rival DICABS is scaling a ₹3,735 Cr backlog leaves zero margin of safety.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: When two-thirds of a quarter's profit jump comes from a one-off oil margin spike, a 42x trailing P/E is actually a 48x–50x multiple on normalized earnings. Never confuse a temporary windfall denominator with a cheap stock.

book_subsections.title: Normalized FY28E Valuation Bridge Reconciled with DCF & Stage 4 Peers
paragraphs: To value Apar honestly, we strip out Q2's ₹23,262/KL TSO spike and model FY27E–FY28E on repeatable unit economics: Specialty Oils reverting to ₹6,500/KL, Conductor EBITDA/MT normalizing to ₹36,500–₹37,000/MT as the ₹12,025 Cr backlog converts, and Specialty Cables compounding at 20%+ toward 11% EBITDA margins. On the post-QIP share count, that yields normalized FY28E EPS of roughly ₹415.

Crucially, we refuse to assign a stretched 37.5x exit multiple while pure-play cable peers trade at 33x–35x in Stage 4. Applying a conservative 33.25x multiple—in line with KEI's 33.09x and below Polycab's 35.29x—yields a blended Base Target of ₹13,800, which reconciles cleanly with our ₹12,300 present-value DCF rolled forward one year at 11.5% WACC (~₹13,715). Our Bull Target sits at ₹17,500 (38.5x FY28E EPS ₹455, matching our DCF Bull) and our Bear Target sits at ₹9,600 (26.3x Bear EPS ₹365, matching our DCF Bear). At ₹14,250 today, Base return is -3.16%.

book_subsections.title: Peer Deconstruction: Sector-Wide Stage 4 Repricing
paragraphs: Look across the November 25 TradingView peer table to see why Apar's pullback is not an isolated mispricing. Polycab India (₹1,12,068 Cr market cap) is down 27.1% from its 52-week high at 35.29x TTM P/E. KEI Industries (₹36,355 Cr market cap) is down 38.1% from its peak at 33.09x P/E. Transformers & Rectifiers (TARIL) trades at 28.39x P/E, and TD Power Systems trades at 54.19x P/E—and every one of them sits in Stage 4.

This mirrors the European grid supercycle parallel of Prysmian and Nexans between 2021 and 2025. Even as Prysmian doubled EBITDA above €1.9 billion, the stock endured repeated 18%–25% valuation drawdowns whenever utility permitting slowed or quarterly mix softened. Paying a 19%–26% P/E premium to Polycab and KEI while total cable exports are down 45.2% YoY (U.S. cable sales -50%) and H1 CFO is negative ₹862.63 Cr is an asymmetric risk you do not need to take.

book_subsections.title: Stress-Testing the Reverse DCF Against Base-Rate Cyclicality
paragraphs: Walk through our Reverse DCF sensitivity matrix to see how little cushion exists at ₹14,250. If Apar compounds normalized NOPAT at 13.5% annually over the next decade—consistent with Conductor EBITDA/MT reverting to ₹32,000–₹34,000/MT and Specialty Oils settling back near ₹5,800/KL—intrinsic equity value falls to ₹40,200 Cr, or ₹9,600 per share (-32.6% downside). Even at a healthy 16.5% ten-year compounding rate with ₹36,000–₹37,000/MT conductor spreads, present intrinsic value is ₹12,300 (-13.7% below CMP).

Only if Apar sustains nearly 20% to 22.5% annual free-cash-flow compounding for ten consecutive years—holding conductor spreads above ₹40,000–₹43,000/MT while scaling Cables at 25%—does today's price look attractive toward ₹17,500. Demanding perfection while H1 operating cash flow is negative ₹862.63 Cr violates core valuation discipline.
